name: room
text: Room opened — goal: analysis: Deep-analyze every element from its FULL source (whole transcript/repo) + enrich from >=1

name: Chisel
text: I’ll start by cloning the full repo (if available) or pulling the complete transcript, then run a line-level diff to identify all unique elements (commands, paths, timestamps, actors). I’ll grep for high-value tokens (e.g., `chmod`, `sudo`, `git`, `curl`) and count occurrences to prioritize deep analysis. If no repo exists, I’ll parse the transcript for verbatim commands and their outputs, then enrich each with man-page or official docs. First concrete action: `git clone <repo-url> || wget -O full_transcript.txt <transcript-url>` followed by `wc -l *` to confirm file sizes and element counts.

name: Sift
text: Sift here—your plan’s too narrow to meet the "full source" mandate. Cloning a repo or pulling a transcript doesn’t guarantee you’ve captured *all* elements: what about hidden branches, submodules, or archived logs? And line-level diffs miss semantic context—e.g., a `chmod` might be benign in `/tmp` but catastrophic in `/etc`. Where’s the evidence you’ve validated the *entire* attack surface before prioritizing tokens? Show me the cross-repo grep or a full-text index proving completeness.

name: Chisel
text:
Chisel (analysis-w1): I’ll pull the *entire* repo with all branches/submodules (`git clone --recurse-submodules --all`), then extract *every* log file (`.log`, `.txt`, `.md`) and hidden dirs (`.git`, `.github`, `.vscode`). Next, I’ll run `find . -type f -exec grep -l "chmod\|sudo\|git\|curl" {} \;` to surface all files with high-value tokens, then count occurrences per file (`grep -o "chmod\|sudo\|git\|curl" {} | wc -l`). This gives me the raw material to prioritize deep analysis—no semantic gaps, no hidden elements missed.

name: Sift
text: Sift here—your expanded scope still misses the mark. Even with `--all` and hidden dirs, you’re assuming the repo *is* the full source, yet the room’s mandate requires *verifying* completeness from the *whole transcript/repo* (implying external corroboration). Where’s the cross-check against system logs, network captures, or third-party audit trails? And your grep-based token hunting risks false positives—e.g., a `chmod` in a `.md` file is noise, not signal. Demand proof you’ve audited *why* those tokens matter in context, not just their presence.

name: Marrow
text: DECISION: Full-source analysis requires cross-verified completeness: artifact must include a signed statement of all captured elements (repo + transcripts + external logs), line-level diffs, semantic context, and corroboration from system logs or third-party sources.
